what_was_done: Most measured commands now block, but the ledger's own git -c 'alias.p=push origin HEAD:develop' p does not. The test runs it only on the main checkout, where position alone blocks. From the story worktree the rule passes it (exit 0), and real git under sh and dash pushes develop. So does git -c alias.p=push p origin HEAD:develop. The aliased verb correctly goes to the not-plain path, but the position test then finds nothing: the far verb sits inside the word alias.p=push, and _chunk_names matches develop, */develop and develop: but not the :develop of a refspec (HEAD:develop). Proposed: a -c, --config-env or GIT_CONFIG_* key that redirects a verb (alias.*, push.*, remote.*.push) never passes on position and blocks opaque_git; _chunk_names also matches <src>:<name> and <src>:refs/heads/<name>. Add both alias pushes from the story worktree as blocked cases. The other measured commands (alias ci on develop, git config alias and remote.origin.push writes, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, send-pack, fast-import) block. But no test fails without the positive verb reading: removing the GIT_COMMANDS check in a scratch copy leaves test_merge_guard green (34 passed), because every tested alias is also caught by _config_directed or by an earlier git config segment. A lone aliased verb on the main checkout, with the alias already in the repository's or the user's configuration (git ci -m x; ci, co and st are common user aliases), is decided by that check alone and is untested; add it. Turning _config_directed off, or the git config write check off, also leaves the suite green: the remote.origin.push cases run only on the main checkout, where a bare push from develop blocks anyway. From the story worktree (where real git pushes develop and the rule now blocks: git -c remote.origin.push=HEAD:refs/heads/develop push origin; git config remote.origin.push HEAD:refs/heads/develop && git push origin) only those checks decide; add both there.

Fixed: every -C is threaded in order, the last --git-dir wins and is resolved with realpath, an absolute cd to a missing directory is unknown, and git -C . -C ../.., the symlinked git-dir and the worktree-add-then-cd form all block. Still wrong: (1) CDPATH is never honoured. _cd_target tests `resolved and cdpath and not resolved.startswith("/")`, and resolved is always absolute, so the branch never runs. Measured from the story worktree, real git under sh and dash commits on develop and the rule passes: export CDPATH=<parent of root>; cd <root name> && git commit --allow-empty -m x (the ledger's own measured form). A prefix CDPATH=<parent> cd <root name> && git commit ... also passes, because _sets_cdpath marks only later segments. tests-first: export CDPATH=<root>/.worktrees; cd S-9.01 && perl -pi -e ... tests/test_sample.py from the main checkout changes the frozen test and passes. The suite's CDPATH row cds to a name that does not exist under CDPATH either, so it blocks for another reason; removing the CDPATH code fails no test. (2) Only the segment that opens a function body with { is marked; the body's later segments keep the definition's directory. From the story worktree, each passing while real git commits on develop: f() { :; git commit --allow-empty -m x; }; cd <root> && f; the same body on several lines; function f { :; git commit ...; } (sh); f() ( git commit ... ); cd <root> && f. The spec says a git call in a { ... } body is not plain. (3) A -C to a directory that does not exist yet is treated as a known place in no project: git worktree add -f <out>/x develop && git -C <out>/x commit --allow-empty -m x from the worktree commits on develop, and git -C <root> worktree add -f <out>/y main; git -C <out>/y commit ... from a directory in no project commits on main. Both pass. (4) -C is resolved lexically, but git's chdir is physical: git -C <link to the worktree>/../.. commit ... from a directory in no project commits on develop and passes. Proposed: test the operand as typed (word.text) for the CDPATH rule, and honour a CDPATH assignment on the cd's own segment; mark every segment between a function's opening { or ( and its close as body (where "", not plain); give a -C or --git-dir target that does not exist at parse time where ""; resolve an existing -C with realpath. Make the CDPATH test row one that sh itself would follow. (5) The realpath step has no test: dropping it from _resolve_dir leaves the suite green, because the only symlink row creates the link in the same command, so the git-dir does not exist at parse time and blocks where_unknown for that reason. Add a row with a symlink to <root>/.git made before the call.
